Suddenly the longing behind my father’s movie is everywhere again, and in 2023 the U.S. Surgeon General even put out an advisory about it. Or about the loneliness under it, at least. They may disagree about politics, food, God, sex, or whether shoes are oppressive, but they agree that something about the current arrangement is starving them.
What's starving them is anomie. We evolved to live in small groups where everybody knows everybody. In a large society the shared norms and close ties that held those groups together fall apart, and that's how large societies end up run by psychopaths. (Yes, I'm always going on about this.)
Check out the Google Trends for “ecovillage” and “intentional community”. After years of decline, interest climbed sharply in the mid-2020s.
I have no proof that the rise of AI caused this turn, but it’s hard to ignore the coincidence in timing. AI became serious around this time, and it started changing people’s jobs and relationships, and how they see the future
